name: Almanac
inspiration: A nineteenth-century almanac: a sun of engraved rays, small-capital headings and a table of the four aspects

name: Signal halo
inspiration: Rings of real hook events radiating from the notch, in a quiet editorial serif on warm paper

name: Night desk
inspiration: A desk late at night: a dark room, a light serif, and the notch's open island casting its state's glow

name: Field manual
inspiration: A technical field manual: condensed capitals, numbered sections, a ruled page and a callout drawing of the notch island

name: Living sky
inspiration: Dusk over a calm harbour: a setting sun, glass panels, and two boats whose wakes glow in their agents' states

name: Session score
inspiration: A musical score of agent sessions: one lane per agent on a timeline, hatched while working, a struck note when it stops

name: Lighthouse
inspiration: A lighthouse at night: the notch is the lamp, its beam sweeps the sea in the current state's colour, and the four states are a chart of lights

name: Departure board
inspiration: A split-flap departures board: every agent session is a row, most urgent first, its status flipping into its state's colour

name: Hi-fi receiver
inspiration: A quiet hi-fi receiver: a speaker grille, four state lamps, a tuning dial for the agents and a row of keys, in warm grey with one orange control

name: Radar scope
inspiration: An approach-control radar scope in cyan phosphor: every agent session is a tagged blip in its state's colour under a turning sweep

name: Riso zine
inspiration: A two-ink risograph zine: fluorescent pink and blue overprinted on cream, misregistered type, halftone dots and a stuck-on sticker

name: Herbarium
inspiration: A naturalist's herbarium: a pressed specimen taped to a mount sheet, its blooms in the four state colours, typed collection labels and pencilled notes

name: Jazz sleeve
inspiration: A mid-century modern jazz LP sleeve: a flat field of blue, huge condensed capitals, a level meter in the state colours, a tracklist and liner notes

name: Contour map
inspiration: A surveyor's topographic sheet: contour lines rising to peaks where each session runs, marked with coloured triangles, a grid, a legend and a scale bar

name: Rose window
inspiration: A cathedral rose window at dusk: rings of leaded stained glass in jewel blues and violets, the state colours set among them and a lit centre

name: Ink tearoom
inspiration: A quiet tearoom scroll: an ensō brushed in sumi ink on washi paper, a vermilion seal, wide margins and a single light where the circle opens

name: Brutalist block
inspiration: A brutalist housing block at night: board-marked concrete, heavy rules, a tower of dark windows where each session is a lit one, and a directory board by the door

name: Deco elevator dial
inspiration: The floor indicator above an Art Deco lift door: a gilt half-dial with a sunburst, a needle that rests on the most urgent state, stepped setbacks and a double frame

name: Lantern street
inspiration: A night-market street strung with paper lanterns: each session is a lantern you read by its colour, under a dusk sky above the rooftops

name: Match day
inspiration: A football pitch on match day: mown stripes, chalk lines, condensed italic numbers and the referee's cards, with every agent a player on the field

name: Bauhaus forms
inspiration: A Bauhaus poster: primary colours on unbleached paper, lowercase geometric type, heavy black rules and one elementary form for each state

name: Diner ticket rail
inspiration: A short-order diner: the service bell on the pass, tickets on a steel rail, an awning stripe, a teal tiled wall and a checkerboard floor

name: Azulejo wall
inspiration: A wall of painted azulejo tiles: cobalt on tin-white glaze with gold rims, read as one pattern until the eye finds the tile that differs

name: Stage cue lights
inspiration: A theatre at curtain-up: velvet curtains, footlights, a gilt line and the stage manager's cue lights, one beam for each state

name: Neon roadside
inspiration: A roadside motel sign at night: a brick wall, hot-pink and cyan tubes, a script wordmark and a stack of signs where the one that matters is lit

name: Illuminated hours
inspiration: A medieval book of hours: vellum, a vermilion rubric, lapis and gold leaf, a vine in the margin, illuminated initials and arched miniatures

name: Signal box
inspiration: A railway signal box at night: an enamelled panel in brass frames, a signal head whose lamp shows the most urgent aspect, and a lever for each state

name: Switchboard
inspiration: A telephone exchange: a walnut cabinet, a jack field with brass rings and lamps, ivory designation strips and key cards, and patch cords

name: Till receipt
inspiration: A shop till's printed receipt on a red counter: every session itemised with its state, the total is free

name: Elevator panel
inspiration: A lift's brushed-steel car panel: a floor dial whose needle points at the most urgent state, and lit call buttons

name: Road signs
inspiration: Roadside signage under an open sky: a blue direction board, white panels with black borders, and a warning shape for each state

name: Punch cards
inspiration: A computer-room desk: manila punch cards with a colour bar for each state, and a green-bar printout of the job

name: Airmail
inspiration: An airmail envelope: striped border, perforated stamps for the four states, a postmark and a typed address

name: Engine telegraph
inspiration: A ship's engine-order telegraph on a night bridge: brass dial, ivory face, a handle that rings the order down

name: Test card
inspiration: A broadcast test pattern: a grey grid, a black circle with a grey step wedge, and four colour bars for the four states

name: Bioluminescence
inspiration: The midwater at night: glowing jellyfish in each state's colour, descending by urgency through marine snow

name: Mineral cabinet
inspiration: A museum mineral drawer: walnut dividers, faceted crystals in each state's colour and typed specimen labels

name: Prism
inspiration: An optical bench on white paper: three agents' beams focused through a lens and a slit, then split by a glass block into Ambient's four state colours

name: Periodic table
inspiration: The classroom periodic table: square cells with atomic numbers and two-letter symbols, the four states as heavy coloured elements

name: Barometer
inspiration: A hallway aneroid barometer: an enamel dial lettered round its arc, a blued needle that swings to the current state, brass rings

name: Honeycomb
inspiration: A brood frame of honeycomb: a beekeeper reads the hive by glancing at the cells, and each lit cell is a session in its state's colour

name: Orrery cyanotype
inspiration: A cyanotype print of a mechanical orrery: white lines in Prussian blue on brushed paper, hand-tinted bodies, caption plates and a plate number

name: Iris
inspiration: An ophthalmic plate of an iris with four sectors of pigment, one per state, a measuring ring and dead-straight annotation leaders

name: Chladni figures
inspiration: Chladni plates: sand on a bowed black plate settles into the figure of its note, one figure and one sand colour per state

name: Petri dishes
inspiration: Petri dishes on a microbiology bench, one culture per state, labelled in marker on torn lab tape

name: Loom
inspiration: A hand loom: each warp stripe is a session dyed in its state's colour, and the beam above shows the most urgent one

name: Glaze tiles
inspiration: A potter's glaze test tiles on a studio shelf: bisque clay, glossy crazed glazes that pool and drip, kiln numbers and pencilled notes

name: Watch dial
inspiration: A chronograph dial: brushed steel case, guilloché centre, four sub-dials and a blued hand that points to the most urgent state

name: Letterpress broadside
inspiration: A wood-type letterpress broadside on yellow stock: fat slab capitals, condensed caps, printer's ornaments and four inks slightly out of register

name: Enamel sign
inspiration: A vitreous enamel sign: cobalt ground, cream border, arrow plates with lamps in the four state colours and the odd chip in the enamel

name: Abacus
inspiration: A counting frame made as a precise instrument: walnut frame, brass rods and corner plates, turned boxwood beads and an engraved scale

name: Chime bars
inspiration: Tuned chime bars on a walnut frame: eight metal bars in the four state colours, brass pins and a mallet striking the one that matters

name: Neon sign
inspiration: An indoor neon blade sign on a bracket against a dark brick wall: bent glass tubes, one lit in the state that matters

name: Zellige
inspiration: A zellige arch: hand-cut glazed eight-pointed stars on plaster, a few glazed in the state colours and a keystone that takes the most urgent

name: Jeweller's tray
inspiration: A jeweller's velvet tray: four faceted stones in gold bezels, one for each state, with hallmarks for what Ambient never does
